description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Authentication' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Authentication — which third-party sign-in methods the title offers and the public OAuth client IDs each platform build needs (currently Google: Web / Android / iOS / Desktop client IDs). Contains NO secrets: OAuth client IDs are public by protocol design, and none of the sign-in flows uses a client secret. Device / e-mail / Telegram / SSO logins need no configuration and are absent from this section. The ID-token audience differs per platform (web and Android tokens carry the Web client ID, iOS tokens the iOS client ID), so several IDs are filled at once and the server accepts any of them.

AppleAuthDefinition.description: Sign in with Apple. No secrets: verifying the identity token needs only Apple's public keys and the audience. The .p8 private key belongs to the authorization-code flow, which is not used here. Unlike Google there is no platform-wide fallback: the audience is the app's bundle ID, which is unique per game.

AdditionalAudiences.description: Extra accepted audiences: a second app of the same team, a build with a different bundle ID, or a migration between identifiers.

BundleID.description: iOS app bundle ID. This is what the native build's token carries in aud.

Enabled.description: Master switch. When false the server rejects Apple login/link and the client hides the button.

ServiceID.description: Services ID — Apple's separate identifier for the WEB flow (with its own return URLs). Web tokens carry it in aud instead of the bundle ID. Empty = no Apple sign-in on the web.

AuthAntiAbuseDefinition.description: Anti-abuse thresholds for authentication. Zero means the platform default, NOT "unlimited".

AccountsPerIpPerDay.description: How many accounts a single IP may create per day. 0 = platform default.

EmailsPerIpPerHour.description: Password-reset e-mails a single IP may trigger per hour. 0 = platform default.

LinkAttemptsPerHour.description: Identity link attempts per player per hour. 0 = platform default.

NativeSsoPollsPerHour.description: Native-SSO request polls per hour. This is the only action the client repeats by design, so the per-second flood limit does not describe it. 0 = platform default.

PasswordAttemptsBeforeLock.description: Failed password attempts before a temporary lock. 0 = platform default.

PasswordLockMinutes.description: How long the temporary password lock lasts, in minutes. 0 = platform default.

RefreshPerHour.description: Session refreshes per hour. 0 = platform default.

VerificationEmailsPerIpPerHour.description: Registration confirmation e-mails a single IP may trigger per hour. Separate from EmailsPerIpPerHour on purpose: registrations must not eat the password-reset quota. 0 = platform default.

AuthEmailDefinition.description: Sender of transactional e-mails. Public part only: no credentials. Empty = platform sender, exactly as before.

PasswordSecretName.description: Name of the TitleSecrets entry holding the SMTP password. Takes precedence over the plaintext password in the private config.

ReplyTo.description: Reply-To address. Worth setting even for a no-reply sender: players do reply, and without it the reply is lost.

SenderEmail.description: From address. Empty = the one configured in the private SMTP settings.

SenderName.description: Display name the player sees in the From field.

TemplateKeyPrefix.description: Localization key prefix for e-mail subjects and bodies. Empty = platform keys.

UseTitleSmtp.description: Send through the title's own SMTP. False = platform sender (settings are kept but unused).

VerificationCodeTtlMinutes.description: Lifetime of the registration confirmation code, in minutes. 0 = platform default.

VerificationMaxAttempts.description: Wrong-code attempts before the code is burnt and a new one must be requested. 0 = platform default.

VerificationResendCooldownSeconds.description: Cooldown between resends of the confirmation code to the SAME address, in seconds. 0 = platform default.

AuthNativeSsoDefinition.description: How the sign-in result gets from the browser back into a NATIVE build. Poll needs no publisher setup and works everywhere; DeepLink returns instantly but requires a URL scheme in both the config and the build. Contains no secrets.

PollIntervalSeconds.description: How often the game should poll for the result, in seconds. A hint for the client so it does not run into the poll quota by accident - the actual limit is NativeSsoPollsPerHour. 0 = platform default.

RequestTtlSeconds.description: How long a Poll-mode sign-in request stays valid, in seconds. This is the window in which the person is expected to finish signing in and come back. 0 = platform default.

ReturnMode.description: Return mechanism: Poll (default, zero setup, works on every platform) or DeepLink (instant, requires a URL scheme registered in the config AND in the build).

UrlScheme.description: App URL scheme without the '://' part, e.g. "mygame". Only used in DeepLink mode. Taken from the config and never from the request - a client-supplied return address would be an open redirect.

AuthSessionsDefinition.description: Session policy of the title: access/refresh lifetimes, concurrent session cap, re-auth window, nonce strictness. Zero means "keep the previous behaviour".

AccessTtlHours.description: Access ticket lifetime in hours. 0 = the previous hardcoded 24h.

MaxConcurrentSessions.description: Max concurrent devices per player. 0 = platform default, which is 1; values above the platform ceiling of 10 are clamped, not refused. When exceeded the OLDEST session is revoked rather than refusing the new login.

ReauthWindowMinutes.description: How recent the login must be for sensitive operations (unlink, revoke-all), in minutes. 0 = platform default.

RefreshTtlDays.description: Refresh token lifetime in days. 0 = platform default.

RequireNonce.description: Require a nonce in Google/Apple tokens. Default false for compatibility: builds already in players' hands do not send one. A nonce that IS sent is always verified regardless of this flag.

GoogleAuthDefinition.description: Google sign-in. The ID-token audience differs per platform, which is Google behaviour and not a choice: Web/GIS and Android/Credential-Manager tokens carry aud = WebClientID, iOS tokens carry aud = IosClientID, loopback/PKCE desktop tokens carry aud = DesktopClientID. The server accepts a token whose aud matches ANY of the filled IDs.

AdditionalAudiences.description: Extra accepted audiences, for migrating between OAuth clients while builds carrying the old client ID are still in players hands.

AndroidClientID.description: Android OAuth client ID. NEVER an ID-token audience (Android tokens carry aud = WebClientID). Kept so the dashboard and the build check can tell the publisher whether their package name + SHA-1 is registered: without that registration Android sign-in fails on the device and leaves no trace on the server.

DesktopClientID.description: Desktop OAuth client ID ("Desktop app" client type) used by the Unity Editor and desktop builds via the system browser + PKCE. Empty = no Editor sign-in.

DisablePlatformFallback.description: Disable the platform-wide fallback client (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID env var). Default false on purpose: the default must mean the behaviour that existed before this section, otherwise adding it would silently break Google sign-in for every existing title.

Enabled.description: Master switch. When false the server rejects LoginWithGoogle / LinkGoogle and the client hides the button.

IosClientID.description: iOS OAuth client ID. Also the source of the reversed-client-ID URL scheme written into Info.plist at build time.

WebClientID.description: Web OAuth client ID. Used by the web build (GIS), by Android (as Credential Manager serverClientId) and optionally by iOS (as serverClientID). Most titles need only this one.

value.description: Title-level authentication settings: which third-party sign-in methods the title offers and the public OAuth client IDs each platform build needs. Contains NO secrets - OAuth client IDs are public by protocol design. Device / e-mail / Telegram / SSO logins need no configuration and are not listed here.

AntiAbuse.description: Abuse thresholds: account creation per IP, password brute-force lockout, e-mail sending caps.

Apple.description: Sign in with Apple configuration (bundle ID for native iOS, Services ID for the web flow).

Email.description: Who transactional e-mails come from. The SMTP password is NOT here - it lives in the private config.

Google.description: Google sign-in configuration (public OAuth client IDs per platform build).

NativeSso.description: Signing in through idosgames.com from NATIVE builds (Android, iOS, desktop). The web and iframe flows need no configuration and are not affected by this block.

Sessions.description: Session policy: token lifetimes, concurrent-device cap, re-authentication window and nonce strictness.
